valueRows.status: implemented by ForgeRuntime; ForgeMap supplies gtfo.player snapshot Data
valueRows.read: ForgeMap/Native/PlayerObservation.cs validates Dam_PlayerDamageBase.Health / HealthMax and publishes RuntimeEntitySnapshot.Health / HealthMaximum; ForgeRuntime ObservationContracts owns the shared budgeted entity.health read.
valueRows.requires: PlayerObservation publishes null health when the receiver is unready, foreign or invalid; the shared Operator accepts gtfo.player | gtfo.enemy and refuses absent Data instead of inventing zero.

ports.fraction: value / maximum, computed by the shared Runtime Operator from the same snapshot

valueRows.read: Dam.Dam_PlayerDamageBase.Infection (System.Single property) for the life the budgeted snapshot read just verified

ports.value: the receiver's infection, in the receiver's own unit (the game publishes no unit)

valueRows.read: the shared snapshot's own LifeState, which the player observer publishes as alive | downed | dead (PlayerObservation.Capture reads PlayerAgent.Alive first and PlayerLocomotion.m_currentStateEnum == PLOC_State.Downed second)
Player.PlayerAgent.Inventory -> Player.PlayerInventoryBase.WieldedItem (Player.ItemEquippable), then RuntimeKernel.ResolveEntity(object) so whichever package owns the item answers
refusals: equipment-unresolved (an item exists but no package names it as an entity — deliberately different from holding nothing)

ports.equipment: the held item's entity, JSON null when the player holds nothing

valueRows.read: Player.ItemEquippable.GetCurrentClip() : System.Int32, GetMaxClip() : System.Int32, GetClassAmmoInPackAbs(SNet_Player) : System.Int32 on the wielded item
refusals: no-wielded-gear (nothing held, so there is no clip)

valueRows.read: Player.PlayerBackpackManager.TryGetBackpack(SNet_Player, out PlayerBackpack) -> PlayerBackpack.Slots[] -> BackpackItem.Instance, then Item.m_expeditionGearComponent != null as the DERIVED test for 'this is the expedition item' (the game exposes no carried flag), then RuntimeKernel.ResolveEntity(object)

ports.item: the carried item's entity, JSON null when nobody in the backpack carries one (a read that happened and found nothing)

valueRows.missing: No native read for a tool's energy or a consumable stack this build can name: Player.ItemEquippable exposes ConsumesBattery() / BatteryConsumption() / OnBatteryLevelChange(Single) (a callback, not a current level) and nothing else about energy, and Player.PocketItem carries only `itemID` — the stack sense of Player.PlayerBackpack.PocketItemsGroups is not established by metadata. No row is registered for it and no value is invented.

actionRows.subject: gtfo.player
actionRows.write: Dam.Dam_SyncedDamageBase.BulletDamage(System.Single dam, Agents.Agent sourceAgent, UnityEngine.Vector3 position, UnityEngine.Vector3 direction, UnityEngine.Vector3 normal, System.Boolean allowDirectionalBonus, System.Single staggerMulti, System.Single precisionMulti, System.UInt32 gearCategoryId) — the packet-sending half of the game's damage path, called on the victim's own receiver
actionRows.confirmation: the receiver's health is read before and after through PlayerHealthReceiver.TryRead; the row reports the health the receiver actually lost (before.Health - after.Health) and an application that landed nothing is an unknown commit, never a success
refusals: damage-kind-unsupported (this entry carries the bullet kind, index 0)

actionRows.subject: gtfo.player
actionRows.status: implemented (ForgeMap binding; the capability row is inserted into CombatContracts by the integration fragment)
actionRows.write: Agents.AgentReplicatedActions.PlayerReviveAction(Player.PlayerAgent p_target, Player.PlayerAgent p_source, UnityEngine.Vector3 where) — an SNet_AuthorativeAction: the host submits it and the game's own validation/apply half (DoPlayerReviveValidation / DoPlayerRevive over pPlayerReviveAction{TargetPlayer, SourcePlayer, Where, setHealthData}) runs on every machine
actionRows.confirmation: the life is read back through the identity: still downed is `revive-not-observed` (unknown commit)
refusals: cost-policy-unsupported (only `none`; the game's revive charges nothing)
source-missing (a reviver that resolves to a player is required)
actionRows.notHonoured: `duration` and `restored_health` are refused by name instead of ignored: the game owns the revive interaction's length and the health a revive restores, and the native entry takes neither.

actionRows.subject: gtfo.player
actionRows.write: Dam.Dam_SyncedDamageBase.SendSetDead(System.Boolean allowRevive) — the host's own replicated transition; the receive half reads pSetDeadData{allowRevive}
actionRows.confirmation: the life is read back through the identity: still alive and not downed is `down-not-observed`. Health is deliberately not the confirmation, because the receiver's own read refuses a life that is no longer alive.

ports.revive_policy: the row's one structural parameter, allowed | denied, submitted as the native entry's own allowRevive argument

actionRows.unverified: Whether SendSetDead(true) leaves the life in the downed state or in the dead state is the game's own locomotion decision and is not readable from metadata: the action reports the write as committed only when the life stopped being alive and not-downed, and the in-game check list carries what state the game actually lands in.

referenceRows.note: These node-list rows land on rows that already exist and are already implemented; this slice registers nothing new for them.
referenceRows.a-p-heal: forge.action.combat.heal for gtfo.player — ForgeMap/PlayerHealthContract.cs + Native/PlayerHealthAction.cs, already registered in MapPluginSession
referenceRows.a-p-teleport: forge.action.player.teleport — ForgeMap/PlayerActionContract.cs + Native/PlayerActions.cs (implemented, registration is the a-player fragment's entry)
referenceRows.a-p-infection: forge.action.player.infection_change — same files, same pending registration
referenceRows.a-p-modifier: forge.action.combat.attribute_apply / attribute_remove for gtfo.player — AgentModifierContract + AgentModifierAdapter, registration is the e-agent-modifier fragment's entry
referenceRows.a-p-ammo: forge.action.inventory.stack_set / forge.action.weapon.ammo_add / ammo_consume are ForgeWeapon's rows (PlayerAmmoStorage, GiveAmmoToPlayer, the ammo sync packet). Nothing is implemented here: a second player-side ammo writer would be a second path to one storage the weapon package already owns.
referenceRows.a-p-item: forge.action.inventory.give / consume / stack_set — the inventory rows are ForgeWeapon's; no ForgeMap binding is registered.
referenceRows.e-p-equip: forge.trigger.input.equipped / unequipped — already declared and already bound; nothing to add.
referenceRows.e-p-downed / e-p-revive: forge.trigger.player.downed / revive_started / revive_cancelled / revived — PlayerLifeContract + Native/PlayerLifeFacts.cs (implemented; registering them is this slice's integration entry).

limits: No game run. The two entries this family's actions submit (BulletDamage, SendSetDead) and the revive action are read from interop metadata; what the game's own receive halves do with them is on the in-game check list together with the quantization of SendSetHealth the existing heal row already documents.
